newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer says Busang bid in Suharto's hands.
newsitem.headline: Placer says Busang bid in Suharto's hands.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc's offer to merge with Bre-X Minerals Ltd is now in the hands of top Indonesian government officials, Placer chief executive officer John Willson said on Tuesday.

"The proposal is with the president and the top mininsters," Willson told analysts in a conference call. "We were not encouraged (by the Indonesian government) to make the proposal," he said. But he said his company had spoken with highly ranked officials before making the offer.
"We have had some discussions with certain people in Indonesia about that," he said.
The Indonesian government has already told Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick Gold Corp and the two companies have been working on a deal for months.
But Willson said on Tuesday that he sensed there is room for another bid.
"We have the sense that there is indeed a green light," he said. "It may not be green, it may be amber."
He would not say who his company had been dealing with in Indonesia or if Placer Dome had struck any local alliances.
Early Tuesday morning, Placer announced it had presented Bre-X with a proposal to marge with Bre-X.

It offered Bre-X a stock-for-stock "merger of equals" at a "significant" premium to Bre-X's current share price under which all of Bre-X's shares would be exchanged for a fixed number of Placer shares.
Willson would not say how many shares it will offer Bre-X shareholders.

The two companies would control 60 percent of the Busang project, while 40 percent would be controlled by the Indonesian government, Indonesian companies and the public, Willson said. Placer would expect some compensation for part of the 40 percent, he said.
"Our proposal has clear benefits to the people of Indonesian and the shareholders of both companies," Willson said.
He said Placer Dome was prepared to finance the US$1.7 billion in capital costs it estimates it would take to bring Busang into production.
"We will reposition our capital spending plans," he said.
The company will be able to take advantage of increased cash flow expected from its Pipeline gold mine in the United States, he added.
Bre-X has not yet responded to Placer Dome's proposal.

Bre-X has said it has a joint proposal with Barrick Gold Corp to form a joint venture to develop Busang. The two companies presented their proposal to the Indonesian government last month, but the deal has not been made final nor the terms made public.

"Time has passed and the reaction of Bre-X shareholders and others to the uncertainty that is inherent in a deal that has not been disclosed has worked on people," said Willson. "We have been encouraged to think a better deal could be brought."
Traders described it as a "bold move."
They estimated that the Placer offer would be worth about C$26 per Bre-X share under Canadian pooling of interest rules.
Placer's first move will be to meet with Bre-X, the Indonesian government and the Indonesian companies involved in Busang to hammer out the terms of an agreement, Willson said.
"I sense that this thing will not be resolved very quickly," he added, saying he does not expect a resolution for at least three months and perhaps six.
Placer would also have to make sure a contract of work is in place for it to go ahead with developing Busang.
"We think Indonesia is not going to issue the contract of work until they see a competent and decent deal," Willson said.
Placer wants to send company officials on to the property at Busang to check Bre-X's numbers and make its own calculations, he said.
Placer Dome suggested production to reach 200,000 tonnes per day, with production starting in 1999. Production could average three to four million ounces of gold per year.
Peak production could be reached after four years of operation, Willson said.
((Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104))
